candidate_075.name: evidential-risk-aware adaptive experiment design
candidate_075.mechanism_hypothesis: Do not optimize experiment selection only for mean expected information gain. Track the distribution of evidential outcomes and penalize designs whose log relative-belief gain is highly variable, because high average information can coexist with a non-vanishing probability of misleading evidence. Use an explicit evidential-risk objective or constraint alongside information gain when selecting sequential experiments.

primary_evidence.source: David Chen, Michael Evans, Xinwei Li, Prateek Bansal, David J. Nott, Deep adaptive design with an evidential bias criterion, arXiv:2608.16466v2, 2026-08-23.
primary_evidence.formal_result: The paper defines bias against BA(x)=P(log RB<=0), the probability under the joint Bayesian model that an experiment produces evidence against the true parameter. It proves and constructs an example where EIG tends to infinity while BA tends to a positive failure probability q, so maximizing average information alone cannot force misleading-evidence risk to zero. The proposed tractable objective is equivalent to maximizing a variance-penalized EIG criterion.
primary_evidence.adaptive_examples: In a 20-step hyperbolic-discounting adaptive design, BA-trained policies preserve very similar mean log relative-belief gain to EIG while reducing its variability and the estimated BA upper bound over the sequence. In the 12-step pizza-choice example, BA likewise keeps mean information similar but lowers evidential variability; its altered design deliberately includes dominated alternatives more often (at least one dominated option frequency 0.4800 vs 0.4182 under EIG), which helps identify context-effect parameters rather than merely balancing choice probabilities.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This adds a distinct control axis to the current acquisition frontier: an experiment can be informative on average yet epistemically dangerous because it has a heavy lower tail of misleading evidence. A scientific controller should therefore reserve a risk budget for experiment designs, not just optimize novelty, uncertainty or expected information.
primary_evidence.limits: This is Bayesian experimental-design methodology, not an end-to-end autonomous scientist benchmark. The examples are simulated/model-based, the risk objective assumes the Bayesian model is itself adequately specified, and the paper does not combine evidential risk with measurement-admissibility, M-open hypothesis expansion, discovery/generalization lanes or live physical-lab execution.

candidate_076.name: discrepancy-gated multi-fidelity experiment allocation
candidate_076.mechanism_hypothesis: Use cheap low-fidelity predictions for broad search, but learn an explicit discrepancy process to the trusted high-fidelity objective. Trigger an expensive real/high-fidelity evaluation only when uncertainty is dominated by the discrepancy term, and update the discrepancy after every paired observation. This turns fidelity choice into a state-dependent gate rather than a fixed cheap/expensive mixture.

primary_evidence.source: Zhuo Chen et al., LABO: LLM-Accelerated Bayesian Optimization through Broad Exploration and Selective Experimentation, arXiv:2605.22054, ICML 2026.
primary_evidence.design: LABO models the real-fidelity objective as a scaled LLM-fidelity process plus a learned discrepancy GP. Its gate uses the discrepancy-dominance ratio p_delta(x)=sigma_delta^2/(rho^2 sigma_L^2+sigma_delta^2) to decide whether a candidate needs a real-fidelity query. Main experiments use the same tau=0.75 across tasks and five random seeds; all methods share GP/RBF/q-UCB machinery and real-fidelity budgets.
primary_evidence.threshold_ablation: On COF, varying tau from 0.60 to 0.85 moves the LLM/real query ratio from 1.52 to 5.26. The intermediate tau=0.75 gives the best final objective 11.228+-0.162 and reaches 90% in 14.17+-6.62 iterations. On Fullerene, the same tau=0.75 gives the best final objective 0.9512+-0.0012 with LLM/real ratio 3.87+-1.62; higher tau=0.85 trusts the low-fidelity source much more (14.60+-3.70 ratio) but slightly worsens the final objective to 0.9499+-0.0010. Thus too much high-fidelity use sacrifices cheap global exploration, while too much low-fidelity trust can mislead search.
primary_evidence.system_results: Across six scientific formula-optimization tasks LABO reports the best overall performance under fixed real-fidelity budgets. In an 86D superconductor task it reports 91.06+-8.05 final objective and 24.4+-23.3 iterations to 90%, versus vanilla BO 57.96+-18.33 and 64.6+-14.3. A random-fidelity ablation converges more slowly and ends worse, and equalizing LLM-suggested initialization does not remove LABO's advantage.
primary_evidence.interpretation: This is direct evidence for dynamic marginal allocation between a broad cheap lane and a costly trusted lane based on measured support/discrepancy, and is stronger than a fixed mixture. It complements candidate_071/072 by giving a concrete state variable for escalation: not raw uncertainty alone, but the fraction of uncertainty attributable to fidelity mismatch.
primary_evidence.limits: The 'real-fidelity' evaluations are benchmark objective evaluations, not necessarily newly executed physical lab experiments. The discrepancy model assumes a KOH-style relationship between fidelities, the main threshold is fixed rather than autonomously calibrated, and the paper does not separate discovery yield from representative/generalization coverage or incorporate measurement-quality admission before fidelity routing.
